messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty HIGH - Elevated DNS failure rate detected for us-east. Synthetic checks show intermittent NXDOMAINs and truncated responses to inference.redwoodapi.com and embeddings.redwoodapi.com. Creating incident thread.

oncall-mei: I'm responding. seeing sudden jump in DNS truncation + EDNS errors from multiple public resolvers starting ~14:12 UTC. App teams report client-side retries and occasional 503s.

netops-jon: pulling up resolver telemetry. Cloudflare recursive cluster in us-east (cf-rec-us-east-2) shows higher-than-normal UDP truncation and fragmentation; packet sizes look borderline. Also seeing increased EDNS DO bit responses toggling.

cloud-eng-amy: can we fail traffic to our Route53 fallback pool and set records to low TTL? I want to avoid client cache poisoning but we need a quick path to restore availability.

support-lee: already seeing top-customer alerts. Estimated impact: ~12% increased errors for hosted inference and embeddings for NA-east customers. Escalating to SEV2. I'll prepare CS blurb.

oncall-mei: short-term mitigation plan: 1) shift geoDNS weights to prefer Route53 fallback pool for us-east. 2) set TTL=20s for affected DNS records. 3) enable TCP-only queries from our resolver proxies as a stopgap. 4) open ticket with CF and add packet captures. Who can make the GeoDNS change?

netops-jon: I can do the weight update and lower TTLs. Executing now. Using the console to up-weight route53-fallback to 85 and set TTL 20s on inference records. Command (console action): UPSERT geodns record set - weight route53-fallback=85 TTL=20.

incident-bot: Probe snapshot: before change - 43% truncated responses to CF recursors, after change - route53-resolved addresses return 98% success from our probes. Refer probe-id 112233.

cloud-eng-amy: also flipping resolver proxy config to prefer TCP for external queries from our network: adding tcp-only flag on forwarders. This will add latency but reduce truncation. Applying to proxy pool now.

netops-jon: posting sample of tcp-forwarder change (sanitized):
```
# update resolv-forwarder config
forwarder {
  name "public-upstream";
  protocol tcp;
  endpoints ["1.1.1.1:53","8.8.8.8:53","3.5.23.10:53"]; # include route53 resolver IPs
}
```

support-lee: sent initial customer message: "We saw a regional DNS degradation in US-East affecting name resolution for our API endpoints. We implemented a GeoDNS fallback to Route53 and additional resolver hardening to restore service. You may have seen transient errors between 14:12-14:28 UTC. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause."

oncall-mei: CF ticket opened via cf-bot: #CF-2026 - attaching our packet captures, EDNS/UDP truncation traces, and probe logs.

cf-bot: Cloudflare support acknowledged ticket CF-2026; initial triage suggests an internal MTU/fragmentation regression on the recursive cluster causing EDNS responses to be fragmented and dropped. CF requested client packet captures and timestamps.

deploy-bot: small deploy just started in us-east for a non-related infra change, pausing rollouts until incident stabilizes.

netops-jon: after GeoDNS shift and TCP enable, app error rates are back to baseline. Monitoring for cache TTL expiry windows.

cloud-eng-amy: action items for post-incident: 1) automate GeoDNS fallback with health checks (weight flip on resolver health), 2) add resolver EDNS/truncation metric to alerting, 3) review TTL strategy for hot records.

oncall-mei: handoff notes to night oncall (@cloud-eng-amy):
- Current state: traffic routed largely to Route53 fallback (weight 85), TTLs 20s, resolver proxies set to TCP-preferred.
- CF ticket open, CF investigating fragmentation on their recursive cluster.
- Monitoring: probe cadence increased to 30s; alert threshold set at 3% resolution failures.
- If CF indicates resolution complete, plan: incrementally reduce weight back to normal over 15 minutes and restore TTLs to 300s after 1h of stable probes.

support-lee: updating customer comms channel with an ETA for next update in 60 minutes. No customers requesting immediate credits; monitoring.

incident-bot: status update - mitigated via GeoDNS fallback and TCP resolver changes. Entering 1h monitoring window.

oncall-mei: leaving detailed runbook notes and all packet captures in the incident ticket. Thanks for the quick responses.

cloud-eng-amy: will follow up with CF and paste their RCA here once available. Scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow.

incident-bot: incident moved to "monitoring" at 14:30 UTC. Full mitigation file attached: probe logs 112233, CF ticket CF-2026, ops run commands.
